physics-killer-09.title: Newton's laws of motion and special relativity
physics-killer-09.topic: Newton's laws of motion and special relativity
physics-killer-09.goal: Analyze the underlying scientific principles and deduce the correct conclusion.
physics-killer-09.material: For nuclear fusion reaction $\mathrm{^2H}+\mathrm{^3H}\rightarrow\mathrm{^4He}+\mathrm{n}$, di mass of each particle na $\mathrm{^2H}$: $2.0141\,\mathrm{u}$, $\mathrm{^3H}$: $3.0160\,\mathrm{u}$, $\mathrm{^4He}$: $4.0015\,\mathrm{u}$, neutron: $1.0086\,\mathrm{u}$. Make di energy wey match $1\,\mathrm{u}$ be $930\,\mathrm{MeV}$, and ignore di kinetic energy of di particles before di reaction. Which one correctly match, in order, di energy $E$ wey di reaction release, and di kinetic energy wey di neutron get if you approximate say di momentum of di $\mathrm{^4He}$ wey form and di neutron get di same size and di mass ratio na $4:1$?
physics-killer-09.thinking.0: Newton's laws of motion and special relativity
physics-killer-09.s.s1.prompt: For nuclear fusion reaction $\mathrm{^2H}+\mathrm{^3H}\rightarrow\mathrm{^4He}+\mathrm{n}$, di mass of each particle na $\mathrm{^2H}$: $2.0141\,\mathrm{u}$, $\mathrm{^3H}$: $3.0160\,\mathrm{u}$, $\mathrm{^4He}$: $4.0015\,\mathrm{u}$, neutron: $1.0086\,\mathrm{u}$. Make di energy wey match $1\,\mathrm{u}$ be $930\,\mathrm{MeV}$, and ignore di kinetic energy of di particles before di reaction. Which one correctly match, in order, di energy $E$ wey di reaction release, and di kinetic energy wey di neutron get if you approximate say di momentum of di $\mathrm{^4He}$ wey form and di neutron get di same size and di mass ratio na $4:1$?
physics-killer-09.s.s1.explain: Because $\Delta m=5.0301-5.0101=0.0200\,\mathrm{u}$, $E=\Delta mc^2=0.0200\times930=18.6\,\mathrm{MeV}$. Di two particles after di reaction get di same momentum size so $K=\dfrac{p^2}{2m}\propto\dfrac1m$ and $K_{He}:K_n=1:4$. So $K_n=\dfrac45\times18.6=14.88\approx14.9\,\mathrm{MeV}$, $K_{He}\approx3.7\,\mathrm{MeV}$. If you write di inverse proportion to mass upside down e be $3.7\,\mathrm{MeV}$ (wrong answer ②), if you divide di energy by half na wrong answer ③, and if you calculate $\Delta m$ wrongly as $0.0400\,\mathrm{u}$ na wrong answer ④.
